newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU non-decision holds up aid to SGS-Thomson.
newsitem.headline: EU non-decision holds up aid to SGS-Thomson.

text.p: The European Commission split on Wednesday over a proposal to block Italy from granting 18 million ecus ($20 million) in research aid to semiconductor producer SGS Thomson, effectively putting the plan on hold.
Ten of the 20 commissioners backed the proposal by Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert -- one short of the number needed to block the aid formally, Commission officials said.
However, Italy cannot grant the money in the absence of a decision.

French EU Research Commissioner Edith Cresson led the opposition to the plan, arguing that U.S. companies were benefiting from more generous research and development aid than Europe's, officials said.
"There was a vote; there was not the necessary majority," Commission spokesman Klaus van der Pas told reporters.

Italy proposed helping SGS-Thomson, a joint venture between Italian industrial state holding IRI and France's Thomson SA, to finance the cost of designing and developing integrated circuits for computer and other applications.
Van Miert argued that the planned grant did not comply with EU rules on state aid to research and development projects since most of the work had already been successfully accomplished.
The Commission agreed to hold a debate on the overall question of how the EU should regulate state aid for research, van der Pas said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
